description: A line-sequential file in cp037 whose records end with 0x15, the byte a mainframe line-delimited file ends a record with. Under the terminator placement a delimiter follows every record, the last included, so three records carry three of them. Two of the three hold a packed amount whose own bytes are 0x15 -- +152.50 is 15 25 0C and +151.50 is 15 15 0C -- so a consumer that searched the input for the delimiter would cut the first record after four bytes and the second after four and again after five. A consumer that counts the extent reads them as the numbers they are.
source: docs/ir/SPEC.md, "Four framings, and none of them is a RECFM", "A delimiter is bytes, not a character", "Terminator, separator, and the last record" and "Where framing is consumed, and where it is emitted"; docs/layout/SPEC.md, "Physical framing" and "A delimiter is bytes, and it has a placement"; the packed amounts are cobol-go codec/SPEC.md Appendix A.4's encoding, and 15 25 0C is the vector docs/ir/SPEC.md itself names
